# Code Style — Python 3.11+ · asyncio · SQLAlchemy 2.0 · Pydantic v2 · PostgreSQL

> Canonical Python coding conventions, reused across projects. Synced into a project's
> `.claude/rules/` by `scripts/sync-code-style.py` — edit the canon here, never the copy
> (wiring: `~/Projects/_shared/17-python-code-style/README.md`). Rationale + sources + which rules are
> verified vs. standard-practice: `~/Projects/_shared/17-python-code-style/SOURCES.md` (paths are absolute because
> this file is copied into projects). Kept lean because it loads into context every session.

## General
- **Clarity over brevity.** Explicit, readable code over clever one-liners.
- f-strings for interpolation (not `%` or `.format()`). `pathlib.Path` over `os.path`.
- Never use a mutable default argument (`def f(x=[])`) — use `None` + set inside.
- `dataclass` for plain internal data; **Pydantic** when you need validation or (de)serialization.

## Formatting & linting
- **Ruff** is the single tool — formatter **and** linter (drop-in for Black + isort + Flake8 +
  pydocstyle + pyupgrade). Format with `ruff format`, lint with `ruff check`.
- Black-style formatting: double quotes, spaces (not tabs), magic trailing commas respected.
- **Line length 88** (Ruff/Black default). Deliberate choice — PEP 8 is 79, Google is 80; 88 is
  least-friction. Set it once in `pyproject.toml` so the linter and this file agree.

## Typing
- Annotate all function arguments and return types. Python ignores annotations at runtime, so
  also run a static checker (**mypy** or **pyright**) in CI — annotations without a checker are
  just documentation.
- **PEP 585 built-in generics:** `list[str]`, `dict[str, int]` — not `List`/`Dict` from `typing`.
- **PEP 604 unions:** `str | None`, not `Optional[str]`; `int | str`, not `Union[int, str]`.
- Avoid `Any`; use precise types or `object`/`Protocol`. Prefer `Protocol` (structural) for
  interfaces over ABCs where it fits.

## Naming (PEP 8)
- `snake_case` — functions, variables, methods, modules, packages.
- `PascalCase` — classes and exceptions.
- `UPPER_CASE` — module-level constants.
- Leading `_` for internal/non-public; descriptive names, no cryptic abbreviations.

## Imports
- Grouped: standard library → third-party → local/first-party, a blank line between groups.
  Enforced natively by Ruff's import rules (`I001`).
- No wildcard imports (`from x import *`). No unused imports.

## Async
- Never block the event loop: no synchronous I/O, `time.sleep`, or CPU-bound work inside an
  `async` function — use async libraries (`asyncpg`, `httpx`), offload blocking I/O via
  `loop.run_in_executor()` (thread pool), CPU-bound work via a `ProcessPoolExecutor`.
- Run independent awaitables concurrently — don't `await` in a loop when calls are independent.
  Prefer **`asyncio.TaskGroup`** (3.11+): if any child raises, it cancels the siblings. `gather`
  with default `return_exceptions=False` propagates the first exception but lets the others keep
  running (weaker). Use `asyncio.timeout()` for deadlines.
- When you catch `asyncio.CancelledError` for cleanup, **re-raise it** — swallowing it breaks
  `TaskGroup`/`timeout`.

## SQLAlchemy 2.0 & PostgreSQL
- **2.0 style**: build `select()`, `await session.execute(stmt)`, then `.scalars()` — not the
  legacy `Query`. Async stack → `create_async_engine("postgresql+asyncpg://…")` + `AsyncSession`
  via `async_sessionmaker(expire_on_commit=False)` (so attributes don't expire into implicit
  lazy I/O after commit).
- **One `AsyncSession` per task** — a session is a single in-progress transaction and is NOT safe
  to share across concurrent tasks (`asyncio.gather`). Keep sessions short-lived, one per
  request/logical operation; `async with session.begin()` per unit of work.
- Avoid N+1: eager-load with `selectinload` (separate IN query, good default) or `joinedload`
  (JOIN) as loader options on the `select()`. Lazy-loading a relationship in async raises — never
  rely on it.
- Migrations via **Alembic**; always review autogenerate output — it misses some changes.

## Pydantic v2
- `BaseModel` for validation/(de)serialization at boundaries (API input, external payloads);
  `BaseSettings` (now in the separate **pydantic-settings** package) for config from env.
- v2 idioms: `model_config = ConfigDict(...)` (not v1 `class Config`); `@field_validator`/
  `@model_validator` (not v1 `@validator`/`@root_validator`); `model_dump()`/`model_validate()`/
  `model_dump_json()` (not `.dict()`/`.parse_obj()`/`.json()`); `Field(...)`.
- Keep Pydantic at the edges; convert to plain/domain objects inside the core if it helps.

## Error handling
- Python is EAFP + exceptions — prefer raising/catching exceptions over Result-return types
  (this is the opposite of the TS guide, and correct for Python).
- Define a project-specific exception hierarchy (a base `AppError`, specific subclasses); raise
  the specific one. Chain with `raise NewError(...) from err` to preserve the cause.
- Never bare `except:` and never a blanket `except Exception:` that swallows — catch the
  narrowest exception you can handle; re-raise or wrap the rest. Never silently `pass` on error.

## Docstrings
- **Google-style** triple-double-quoted docstrings (PEP 257) with `Args:`/`Returns:`/`Raises:`
  on public functions, classes, and modules. Skip docstrings on trivial/obvious internals.
